main_text.p: Ætas segetes, sævum mare, bibulam arenam, pedem montis, & sexcenta quotidie similia, inter confabulandum effundimus: quæ clarè arguunt, nos personam nostram rebus inanimis, in scena vehementiorū affectuum ac familiarium sermonum sæpe admodum imponere. Hoc amplius: Simias, bubones, ranas, deformes & turpes animantes esse, passim asseveramus: quid ita? cur potius hac infamiæ notâ inuruntur, quam equi, oves, galli? Nimirum propter majorem nobiscum in figura similitudinem, tum etiam (quod præsertim in similis valet) propter similes quasdam gesticulationes, facilius quam animantes aliæ in humanum genus adoptantur, intra quod imaginationis ope consistentes deficiunt, & conspicuo formæ ab hominibus, cum quibus componebantur, recessu, fiunt monstrosæ: quo utique probro non laborarent, si in familia sua per-

page.notes: The first letter of "Ætas" is partly cut by the edge of the page, so the reading is slightly uncertain. The left margin has only fragments of the neighbouring page and no printed note on this page. The paragraph continues on the next page at "per-". The sentence is mostly set in italic type, which is shown as roman here because the transcription was made from the visible letters without marking italics.
